body:
The simulator ports do not compile when `TX_MISRA_ENABLE` is defined.

`_tx_thread_stack_build()` in all four simulator ports uses
`TX_POINTER_TO_ALIGN_TYPE_CONVERT()` and `TX_ALIGN_TYPE_TO_POINTER_CONVERT()`:

- `ports/linux/gnu/src/tx_thread_stack_build.c`
- `ports/win32/vs_2019/src/tx_thread_stack_build.c`
- `ports/win64/vs_2022/src/tx_thread_stack_build.c`
- `ports_smp/linux/gnu/src/tx_thread_stack_build.c`

`common/inc/tx_api.h` defines both macros only in the **non-MISRA** branch, at lines
2006-2007, inside the `#else` that begins at line 1990. The `#ifdef TX_MISRA_ENABLE`
branch above it (lines 1884-1990) defines no equivalent pair, so with `TX_MISRA_ENABLE`
defined the two names are undeclared and the translation unit fails to compile.

## Reproduction

On `dev` at 9e4c5713:

```
gcc -m32 -c -DTX_MISRA_ENABLE -I common/inc -I ports/linux/gnu/inc \
    ports/linux/gnu/src/tx_thread_stack_build.c -o /dev/null
```

```
ports/linux/gnu/src/tx_thread_stack_build.c:128:23: error: implicit declaration of function
  'TX_POINTER_TO_ALIGN_TYPE_CONVERT'; did you mean 'TX_POINTER_TO_ULONG_CONVERT'?
ports/linux/gnu/src/tx_thread_stack_build.c:130:42: error: implicit declaration of function
  'TX_ALIGN_TYPE_TO_POINTER_CONVERT'; did you mean 'TX_ULONG_TO_POINTER_CONVERT'?
ports/linux/gnu/src/tx_thread_stack_build.c:130:39: error: assignment to 'VOID *' {aka 'void *'}
  from 'int' makes pointer from integer without a cast
```

The same command without `-DTX_MISRA_ENABLE` compiles cleanly.

## How it got in

The two macro calls arrive with d3fb72b6 (#705), which aligns the fake stack pointer so
the ports stop performing misaligned `ULONG` accesses. That fix is correct and worth
keeping; only its choice of conversion macros is the problem.

No build configuration in `test/tx/cmake` or `test/smp/cmake` defines `TX_MISRA_ENABLE`,
so CI does not compile these files in that mode and did not catch it. It surfaced on the
`v6.4.1_cert` branch, which carries an extra `TX_MISRA_ENABLE` build configuration.

## Suggested fix

Two options, either of which resolves it:

1. Write the conversions inline, as the surrounding code already does. This keeps the
   change inside the port and needs no header edit:

   ```c
   fake_stack_ptr =  (ALIGN_TYPE) ((VOID *) (((CHAR *) thread_ptr -> tx_thread_stack_end) - 8));
   fake_stack_ptr =  fake_stack_ptr & (~((ALIGN_TYPE) (sizeof(ULONG) - 1)));
   thread_ptr -> tx_thread_stack_ptr =  (VOID *) ((ALIGN_TYPE) fake_stack_ptr);
   ```

2. Add a MISRA-branch definition of the two macros in `common/inc/tx_api.h`, alongside the
   `_tx_misra_*` conversion helpers, so the names exist in both modes.

Option 1 is what the `v6.4.1_cert` branch uses, verified to build and pass in six
configurations including the `TX_MISRA_ENABLE` one. Note that substituting the `ULONG`
pair is not equivalent: on this port `ALIGN_TYPE` is `unsigned long long` on `__x86_64__`
while `ULONG` is 32-bit, so a `ULONG` round trip would truncate the pointer.

## Worth considering separately

Adding a `TX_MISRA_ENABLE` build configuration to the regression CMake would stop this
class of defect recurring. It compiles `common/src/tx_misra.c` and the six `*_initialize.c`
files that `TX_INLINE_INITIALIZATION` empties on the simulator ports, none of which any
current configuration builds.
title: Simulator ports do not compile when TX_MISRA_ENABLE is defined
